verses.1: A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.
verses.2: How many are my foes, LORD! How many rise against me!
verses.3: How many say of me, "God will not save that one." Selah
verses.4: But you, LORD, are a shield around me; my glory, you keep my head high.
verses.5: Whenever I cried out to the LORD, I was answered from the holy mountain. Selah
verses.6: Whenever I lay down and slept, the LORD preserved me to rise again.
verses.7: I do not fear, then, thousands of people arrayed against me on every side.
verses.8: Arise, LORD! Save me, my God! You will shatter the jaws of all my foes; you will break the teeth of the wicked.
verses.9: Safety comes from the LORD! Your blessing for your people! Selah

notes.text: The superscription, added later, relates the psalm to an incident in the life of David.
Selah: the term is generally considered a direction to the cantor or musicians but its exact meaning is not known. It occurs 71 times in 39 psalms.
